handoff: review#3: AC1-AC4 proven at S1; review#2 R2-F1..F10 all hold; no blocking findings; minors R3-F1 (seen counts unapplied receipts), R3-F2 (rejected.json RMW without lock), R3-F4; nits R3-F3, R3-F5; D17 empty boundary commits for the person at the ready gate

findings.title: `seen` counts unapplied receipts
findings.detail:
keptRejection sets seen = nextReceiptNumber(u) - 1, which includes receipts not yet applied. A local answer that is unapplied when a stale mailbox receipt is rejected does not clear the item once it is applied a tick later (r.n > seen is false). The item stays until the next answer or approval, or until the story finishes. An edge of B21's 'a later answer … is accepted'.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Use applied_through for seen.

findings.title: rejected.json read-modify-write without a lock; one bad entry empties the file
findings.detail:
addRejectedReceipt and pruneRejectedReceipts read, change and rewrite the file. A tidy racing a tick can lose one write. If one entry fails validation, the whole file reads as empty (the S2 fallback), and the next add overwrites every open rejection.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Take the tick lock in tidy's prune (or check that it already holds it), and validate entry by entry.

findings.title: `rejected_receipts` is always in tidy's output
findings.detail:
The key is present even when empty, while the herdr key next to it is left out when there is nothing to report.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Leave it out when empty.

findings.title: The tidy test reads rejected.json directly
findings.detail:
D12 allows it (the file is kept machine-local), but the tidy JSON output and checkItems would observe the same behaviour without reaching into the file.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Optional: assert through tidy's output and the inbox.

findings.title: The variable `answer` holds reject events
findings.detail:
Naming only.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Rename it to `rejects`.
